task.title: Configuring Red Hat Quay to use Splunk
task.shortdesc: To send Red Hat Quay action logs to Splunk or the Splunk HTTP Event Collector (HEC), you can add the Splunk settings to your config.yaml file and restart the registry.

ul.li: You have installed Splunk and created a username.
You have generated a Splunk bearer token.

step.cmd: Configure Red Hat Quay to use Splunk or the Splunk HTTP Event Collector (HEC).

substep.cmd: If opting to use Splunk, open your Red Hat Quay config.yaml file and add the following configuration fields:

info.codeblock: # ... LOGS_MODEL: splunk LOGS_MODEL_CONFIG: producer: splunk splunk_config: host: http://<user_name>.remote.csb port: 8089 bearer_token: <bearer_token> url_scheme: <http/https> verify_ssl: False index_prefix: <splunk_log_index_name> ssl_ca_path: <location_to_ssl-ca-cert.pem> search_timeout: 60 max_results: 10000 export_batch_size: 5000 # ...

dlentry.dd: Specifies the Splunk cluster endpoint.
Specifies the Splunk management cluster endpoint port. Differs from the Splunk GUI hosted port. Can be found on the Splunk UI under Settings → Server Settings → General Settings.
Specifies the generated bearer token for Splunk.
Specifies the URL scheme for access the Splunk service. If Splunk is configured to use TLS/SSL, this must be https.
Specifies whether to enable TLS/SSL. Defaults to True.
Specifies the Splunk index prefix. Can be a new, or used, index. Can be created from the Splunk UI.
Specifies the relative container path to a single .pem file containing a certificate authority (CA) for TLS/SSL validation.
Specifies the timeout for Splunk search queries in seconds. Increase for slow Splunk clusters or complex queries.
Specifies the maximum number of results to return per search query. Larger values require more memory.
Specifies the batch size for log export operations.

substep.cmd: If opting to use Splunk HEC, open your Red Hat Quay config.yaml file and add the following configuration fields:

info.codeblock: # ... LOGS_MODEL: splunk LOGS_MODEL_CONFIG: producer: splunk_hec splunk_hec_config: host: prd-p-aaaaaq.splunkcloud.com port: 8088 hec_token: 12345678-1234-1234-1234-1234567890ab url_scheme: https verify_ssl: False index: quay splunk_host: quay-dev splunk_sourcetype: quay_logs timeout: 10 search_token: <bearer_token> search_host: <splunk.example.com> search_port: 8089 search_timeout: 60 max_results: 10000 export_batch_size: 5000 # ...

dlentry.dd: Specifies splunk_hec when configuring Splunk HEC.
Specifies the logs model configuration for Splunk HTTP Event Collector action logs configuration.
Specifies the Splunk cluster endpoint.
Specifies the Splunk management cluster endpoint port.
Specifies the HEC token for Splunk.
Specifies the URL scheme for access the Splunk service. If Splunk is behind SSL/TLS, must be https.
Specifies whether to enable (true) or disable (false) SSL/TLS verification for HTTPS connections.
Specifies the Splunk index to use.
Specifies the host name to log this event.
Specifies the name of the Splunk sourcetype to use.
Specifies the timeout in seconds for HTTP requests to the Splunk HEC endpoint. Prevents requests from hanging indefinitely when Splunk is unresponsive.
Specifies an optional bearer token for the Splunk search API. Required because HEC tokens are ingest-only and cannot search.
Specifies the Splunk management host for the search API. Defaults to the HEC host if not specified.
Specifies the Splunk management port for the search API. Defaults to 8089 if not specified.
Specifies the timeout for Splunk search queries in seconds. Increase for slow Splunk clusters or complex queries.
Specifies the maximum number of results to return per search query. Larger values require more memory.
Specifies the batch size for log export operations.

step.cmd: If you are configuring ssl_ca_path, you must configure the SSL/TLS certificate so that Red Hat Quay trusts it.

substep.cmd: If you are using a standalone deployment of Red Hat Quay, SSL/TLS certificates can be provided by placing the certificate file inside of the extra_ca_certs directory, or inside of the relative container path and specified by ssl_ca_path.
If you are using the Red Hat Quay Operator, create a config bundle secret, including the certificate authority (CA) of the Splunk server. For example:

info.codeblock: $ oc create secret generic --from-file config.yaml=./config_390.yaml --from-file extra_ca_cert_splunkserver.crt=./splunkserver.crt config-bundle-secret
info.p: Specify the conf/stack/extra_ca_certs/splunkserver.crt file in your config.yaml. For example:
info.codeblock: # ... LOGS_MODEL: splunk LOGS_MODEL_CONFIG: producer: splunk splunk_config: host: ec2-12-345-67-891.us-east-2.compute.amazonaws.com port: 8089 bearer_token: eyJra url_scheme: https verify_ssl: true index_prefix: quay123456 ssl_ca_path: conf/stack/splunkserver.crt # ...
